title: Cabin Window Assembly — Frame Land Repair after Sealant Corrosion at the Window Belt

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Windows — Cabin Window Assembly

abstract: Repair of the cabin window frame land after corrosion under a degraded sealant bead, restoring the sealing face and the frame fastener land without replacing the window frame structure.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the cabin window frame land and its sealing face after corrosion has developed under a degraded sealant bead, without removing the window frame from the fuselage.
sections.damage_assessment: Remove the cabin lining and the window reveal to expose the frame land. Remove the sealant bead completely and clean the land. Map the corrosion depth with an ultrasonic thickness gauge at the twelve positions given in the instructions. Corrosion inside the blend limit may be blended and re-protected without this repair. Corrosion that reaches the frame fastener land, corrosion that has spread to the adjacent window bay, or any evidence of cracking at a fastener hole is outside the scope and requires an engineering assessment. Inspect the two adjacent windows at the same time; corrosion at a window belt is almost never confined to one bay and repairing a single window usually means returning to the same aircraft within a year.
sections.repair_procedure: Blend the corrosion to a smooth depression with a minimum radius of 8 millimetres and confirm by dye penetrant that no indication remains. Machine the doubler seat in the frame land so that the doubler sits flush with the sealing face. Prepare the faying surfaces and apply the chromate-free protection to all bare material. Fit the strap D5620114557898 dry and check the fit with a feeler gauge over its whole footprint. Install the fasteners wet with sealant to the pattern on repair drawing RD-56-20-11-915, working from the centre outwards. Where the doubler reaches the rib D5620115932327, use the shorter fastener on sheet 2. Apply the new sealant bead to the section given on the drawing and tool it to the profile shown; a bead that is proud will be nipped by the window reveal and will fail again in the same way. Let the sealant cure for the full period and then do a pressure check of the window bay. Refit the reveal and the cabin lining.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of the sealant bead and the doubler edge at every cabin refresh and at every C check. An ultrasonic thickness check of the repaired land is required every 10000 flight cycles. Any new corrosion under the bead, any sealant separation at the reveal, or any pressure leakage at the window bay makes the repair invalid. The repair is not life limited provided the inspection programme is followed and the bead is renewed at each cabin refresh.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Corrosion up to 10 per cent of the nominal frame land thickness over an arc not larger than 120 millimetres, not reaching the frame fastener land and not extending into the adjacent window bay.
